Turn in all of your notes and event materials when you have completed the event.
situation:
You are the marketing manager for SHINE ROUTE MOBILE DETAILING, a profitable mobile car detailing business that washes and polishes vehicles at customers' homes and offices. The founder (judge) built the company over eleven years and is preparing to exit at the close of this quarter, selling it to the six crew members who work in it.

The sale closes as a new legal entity under a new name, because the agreement takes the founder's name off the trucks. The new company opens with no history of its own: it must set up its own books, keep records of every expense, and make its first quarterly tax payment ninety days after it opens. The crew members are putting their savings into the purchase, and the fleet accounts on standing monthly contracts booked with the founder personally and have not been told the business is changing hands.

One launch fund is left, and it covers either a paid advertising campaign or the bookkeeper and the first quarterly tax payment, not both. Spending it on radio spots and a press announcement introduces the new name across the region, and it costs the new company the bookkeeper and the money set aside for that first quarterly tax payment. Keeping it for the bookkeeper and the tax payment holds the relaunch to free social posts and the founder's personal referrals, and it costs the new name any paid visibility while leaving the brand attached to a founder who is walking away.

The founder (judge) has asked you to scan the local market and the competing detailers, explain what the advertisements would contain, identify the public-relations activities the relaunch could use, explain how promotion would shape the new brand, and recommend a positioning concept for the fleet-care plan the company wants to introduce.

The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the founder's questions, the founder (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of SHINE ROUTE MOBILE DETAILING. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are leaving at the close of the quarter, and the six crew members buying the company will live with whatever is decided now. You want the marketing manager to scan the local market and the competing detailers, explain what the advertisements would contain, identify the public-relations activities available for the relaunch, explain how promotion would shape the new brand, recommend a positioning concept for the fleet-care plan, and tell you plainly whether the launch fund should go to the campaign or to the bookkeeper and the first quarterly tax payment.

After the marketing manager has presented, you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what would tell you this was the right call?
What would you watch in the first three months to know whether it is working?
